items.reason: Inclusion admits 'both IDHwt GBM and IDHm Grade 4 astrocytoma' with a separate 'IDHm Grade 4 astrocytoma arm'; IDH-mutant grade 4 astrocytoma is not glioblastoma under CNS5, so more than one glioma type is eligible and GBM is named.

The record calls the population 'GBM ... including both IDHwt GBM and IDHm Grade 4 astrocytoma', i.e. it explicitly allows IDH-mutant tumours under the GBM label (historical); it neither requires IDH-wildtype for GBM nor cites WHO CNS 2021. Low-medium because it does use CNS5 terms ('IDHm Grade 4 astrocytoma').
D31-C2 lists every other drug given with the candidate, co-candidates included: 'STAR-001 in combination with the oral diuretic spironolactone' in every experimental arm.

Tumour tissue is collected 'for retrospective exploratory biomarker analysis and determination of intertumoral PTGR1 levels', a planned biomarker not linked in the record to STAR-001 or its target, which the manual codes unclear.

note: Spironolactone is a candidate as a tumour chemosensitiser ('a transcription-coupled nucleotide excision repair (TC-NER) inhibitor, sensitized GBM cells'), consistent with D30-R6. Both coders listed IDH as an enrichment biomarker (not queued); I propose any_molecular_selection false because IDH status here only defines the two diagnostic cohorts (IDHwt GBM vs IDHm grade 4 astrocytoma), not a molecular selection; XL may prefer the coders' derived value (true). D31-A1/A5 support any_molecular_selection false: the IDH-mutant requirement applies only to the non-GBM 'IDHm Grade 4 astrocytoma arm' (GBM patients enter without it), and IDH-wildtype only defines GBM.
